overview.problemStatement: Every multi-provider product reinvents tenant identity, provider identity, capability shape, and token storage, so consumers invent incompatible models and downstream crates such as quota-ledger and hookgate cannot share a tenant.
overview.proposedSolution: Port and adapt the existing platform-core crate from feature/m3-substrate: TenantId, ProviderId, ProvisioningMode, Capability, the Provider trait, an explicit Registry, and an async TokenStore with MemoryTokenStore. Standalone trait crate; no OAuth, quota, webhook, or product vocabulary.
overview.targetAudience: Rust teams building a multi-tenant product on provider crates, and this project's quota-ledger and hookgate features.
assumptions: A working implementation exists on feature/m3-substrate (14 files, features registry and memory) and is ported rather than redesigned.
main has no workspace.dependencies, so async-trait, secrecy, thiserror, and uuid are declared directly in the crate manifest.
The branch tests are not ported; the test agent authors tests against this specification.
The unmerged m3-substrate/v1 spec covers four crates and is not reused as governance here.
outOfScope: OAuth flows, token refresh, and provider clients.
Database or HTTP framework features in 0.1.
Product nouns and vendor workflow code (CON-106).

userStories.title: Identify tenants and providers
userStories.want: value types for tenant and provider identity
userStories.benefit: every crate in the stack speaks the same identity model

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the crate built with --no-default-features, when it compiles, then identity, error, and token modules are available without the registry.
Given TenantId and ProviderId, when used, then both are cheap value types wrapping Uuid and a static str with Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, and Hash.
Given a provider provisioning path, when ProvisioningMode is inspected, then it distinguishes Api, Partner, Manual, and Unsupported.

userStories.title: Describe capabilities
userStories.want: providers to publish what they can do
userStories.benefit: a router can reason about capability without knowing the vendor

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a Provider implementation, when capabilities() is called, then it returns a static slice of Capability values pairing an opaque key with a ProvisioningMode.
Given a capability key, when it is compared, then the crate treats it as opaque and defines no product vocabulary (CON-106).

userStories.title: Register providers explicitly
userStories.benefit: provider wiring is visible and testable instead of global

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an empty Registry, when a provider is registered, then get, iter, and capabilities return it.
Given a registry already holding a provider id, when the same id is registered again, then registration fails with a typed error naming the duplicate id.
Given the crate, when its public surface is inspected, then there is no global mutable singleton and no static mut (CON-109).

userStories.title: Store tokens behind a contract
userStories.benefit: storage and key management stay in my adapter

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a TokenStore implementation, when get, put, and revoke are called, then they are async and keyed by the tenant and provider pair.
Given the memory feature, when MemoryTokenStore is used, then it satisfies the trait and is absent when the feature is off.
Given a stored secret, when it is formatted with Debug, then the value is redacted and no plaintext token appears.
Given a token-store failure, when it is returned, then it is a TokenError with a stable message and no secret material.
Given the crate, when it is built on Rust 1.85 with all features, then it compiles with forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs) and ships the licence files.

functionalRequirements.text: The crate MUST expose TenantId, ProviderId, ProvisioningMode, Capability, Provider, Registry, TokenStore, TokenError, and Secret per catalogue/31_platform_core.md.
Features MUST be additive and default to registry plus memory; a --no-default-features build MUST compile.
Registry MUST reject a duplicate provider id with a typed error naming the id.
Registration MUST be explicit and the crate MUST NOT expose a global mutable registry.
TokenStore MUST be async, keyed by tenant and provider, and cover get, put, and revoke.
MemoryTokenStore MUST be gated behind the memory feature.
Secrets MUST render redacted in Debug output.
Errors MUST carry stable messages with no secret material.
The ported crate MUST declare forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs) and include the licence files.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Tenant data MUST be isolated by the tenant and provider key; no API may return another tenant's token (CON-512).
Credentials MUST come from the caller's TokenStore implementation and the crate MUST NOT read the environment (CON-519).
The crate MUST compile on Rust 1.85 with all features (CON-102).
The public surface MUST contain no product vocabulary and no vendor workflow code (CON-106).
Every public item MUST carry rustdoc and every module MUST state scope and non-goals (CON-202, CON-203).

edgeCases.description: Registering the same provider id twice
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Typed error naming the id; the registry is unchanged.

edgeCases.description: get for an absent tenant and provider pair
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Returns Ok(None); never a fabricated token.
Identity, error, and token modules compile without the registry.
Redacted placeholder appears; never the value.

dependencies.notes: Async TokenStore methods; declared directly because main has no workspace.dependencies.

dependencies.name: secrecy
dependencies.notes: Redacted Secret wrapper; pin one major.

dependencies.name: tokio
dependencies.notes: Dev only, for async token-store tests written later by the test agent.

risks.description: Porting stale code may drag in APIs that no longer match the workspace, since the branch predates wirekit.
risks.mitigation: Port file by file, adapt the manifest, and let the MSRV and clippy jobs prove it.
Pin one major and cover redaction with AC-011.

risks.description: A trait crate invites scope creep into implementations.
risks.mitigation: NFR-004 and the out-of-scope list are enforced at review.
